slides.texte_overlay:
unusual things truly confident
people do in public

they choose the visible seat

they sit in the middle of the room instead of hiding in a corner. picking a seat where people can see you, without making a fuss, is a quiet sign of ease.

they eat slowly

they enjoy their food at their own pace, even when everyone else is rushing. not matching other people's speed shows they're comfortable in their own rhythm.

they let pauses happen

a few seconds of silence after they speak doesn't bother them. they don't rush to fill it, and that calm makes everything they say feel more important.

they keep learning

confident people stay curious about everything and learn something small each day, a strange fact or a famous painting. that steady growth keeps them calm and sure.

slides.texte_overlay:
they ask for clarity

they say sorry, what do you mean, without any embarrassment. asking someone to explain instead of nodding along is something only secure people really do.
